feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV for a senior digital communications leader: clear positioning, credible progression, and relevant platform/strategy depth. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing scope from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong relevance for digital strategy roles, with credible expertise across Drupal, analytics, governance, email, social, and multimedia.  
- Good use of concrete scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers), which boosts credibility.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond activity/scope: e.g., traffic growth, email performance, engagement gains, cost savings, efficiency improvements, adoption rates.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to sharpen structure and save space.  
- Fix minor writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; add serial commas consistently (“content operations, and enterprise web improvement” vs other lists); “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “French (basic working proficiency).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, tighter phrasing, and a few specifics that reflect the most recent Drupal, analytics, and governance work.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with “multi-channel digital communications” to reduce list fatigue.
- Add 1–2 high-value differentiators from recent roles, such as Drupal platform modernization, analytics/governance, or mission-driven membership organizations.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years’ experience leading multi-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in web and CMS modernization, cross-channel content operations, analytics, and digital governance. Strong track record in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating complex policy or technical issues into clear, accessible communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and “stakeholder coordination” repeat language already covered in Core Competencies and Soft Skills.
- Avoid adding too many platform/tool details here; those are already well covered in Topline Skills and Technical + IT.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership/strategy capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “CMS modernization,” “Editorial governance,” “Analytics & performance reporting.”
- Group related items and reduce filler: “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” → “Cross-functional stakeholder leadership.”
- Prioritize the most marketable, recent strengths from experience: web platform modernization, digital operations, analytics, advocacy communications, multimedia production.
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise digital strategy • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial governance & workflow design • Cross-channel communications leadership • Analytics, KPI reporting & optimization • Digital systems architecture • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with Header and Topline Skills; consider shortening this section or using it only if the CV format requires it.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also repeats Soft Skills almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo roles below and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level scope, strategic outcomes, and only the newest/highest-value work.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, web governance, campaign architecture, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-focused bullets; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one line about improving cross-channel communications operations.
- Rephrase execution bullets to show outcomes: “Built Drupal campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and member toolkits to support advocacy and engagement” and “Delivered front-end/CMS enhancements for high-traffic public web properties.”
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search relevance gains, engagement/download metrics.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Drupal microsites,” “AI-enabled search,” and “campaign storytelling” duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this item higher-level and let projects hold specifics.
- “Governance, analytics, workflows” also repeats the 2022–2024 Director role; emphasize advisory/consulting scope rather than re-listing prior responsibilities.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals; it will be even stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with a sharper scope/result summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to emphasize highest-impact achievements first: Drupal migration, analytics stack expansion, in-house studio build, governance/operations improvements.
- Add outcome language where possible: site performance gains, publishing efficiency, reporting speed, cost savings from in-house production, engagement growth, or reduced reliance on vendors.
- Tighten channel bullet: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders” rather than listing generic platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version strategic, not operational.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo roles and footer projects; emphasize building the studio/capability, not recurring content production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Emphasize what changed under your ownership: scale, cadence, cross-team coordination, and channel-building.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: newsletter ownership, launch/expansion of recurring advocacy video, and cross-functional editorial planning.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: newsletter send volume/open rates, video cadence/views, number of teams/stakeholders coordinated, or workflow time saved.
- Possible rewrite:
- Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, supporting advocacy campaigns and coordinated editorial execution.
- Owned four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Improved cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications across web, email, social and video” is repeated in the Director role; keep this version more execution-focused.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value leadership capabilities not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise web and communications strategy”; “Multi-channel communications leadership” → “Cross-channel communications operations.”
- Add one more distinctive capability tied to recent work, such as “Content governance and publishing standards” or “AI-enabled content discovery strategy.”
- Keep to 4 bullets max and use parallel noun phrases for cleaner scanning.
- Suggested rewrite:
- Enterprise web and communications strategy
- Content governance and editorial systems
- Cross-channel communications operations
- Public-sector advocacy and audience strategy

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker and partly redundant with “editorial systems,” “communications operations,” and the header’s “content operations.”
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with Core Competencies; consider “public-sector advocacy strategy” if retained.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes, not repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS leadership • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Prioritize the most current, proven strengths from recent roles: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/workflows.
- Remove lower-signal or less evidenced items here if space is tight, especially “WordPress,” “SharePoint,” and “Power Pages,” since they are already covered in Technical + IT.
- If you want more impact, make one item outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” or “AI-enabled search for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also repeats Core Competencies almost verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT” and reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + tools: “Analytics infrastructure and optimization” or “Analytics, reporting & performance optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity” instead of listing each separately.
- Replace generic phrases with stronger business language: “KPI framework development” and “executive reporting dashboards” are sharper than “KPI design” and “Leadership reporting.”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive reporting dashboards • SEO, UX and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “Performance analysis” may overlap with Core Competencies’ “Analytics and reporting infrastructure.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value production leadership and event delivery rather than basic task labels.

- Replace with more outcome-oriented, senior phrasing:

- If space is tight, cut to 4 bullets and keep the most distinctive items: studio buildout, livestream/hybrid events, multi-camera systems, advocacy video delivery.

- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies.
- Tool-level production details are also partially covered under Technical + IT (“Livestream studio workflows,” podcast production).

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should either add context on level of use or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, prioritize by depth/relevance: **Drupal • SharePoint • WordPress • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider dropping the title “Web Platforms & CMS” in favor of **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.
- Only keep platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; Drupal is clearly the strongest and should lead.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates the “Topline Skills” entry: **Drupal - WordPress - SharePoint - Power Pages**. Differentiate this section with proficiency/context or remove one version.
- GitHub Pages is not reinforced elsewhere; keep it only if it supports a concrete project or technical positioning.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw languages to capability-based phrasing: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless ATS targeting requires them; “HTML/CSS” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add scope or outcomes in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., implementations supporting Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, or workflow automation.
- Order by strongest/current value: JavaScript • API integrations • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • Google Tag Manager • HTML/CSS • jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- Google Tag Manager may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” if that section needs more specificity.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize systems actually tied to recent leadership work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- Remove lower-signal tools unless actively used recently: **Basecamp, Trello**
- If accurate, add light context instead of pure listing: **Airtable (workflow systems), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana (project operations), Slack/Teams (cross-team coordination)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; keep this section tool-focused, not capability-focused.
- Collaboration apps like Slack/Teams can feel low-value on a senior CV unless framed as part of operational systems.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations, but it reads as a generic tool list. Strengthen it by signaling enterprise-scale email/engagement capability and aligning wording with the more senior recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Replace with: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic Thrive Marketing • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope-oriented phrasing elsewhere in the skills section, e.g. “enterprise email automation,” “newsletter operations,” or “member communications platforms” rather than just vendor names.
- Keep only the strongest/current systems; order by recent or most enterprise-relevant platform first.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with repeated “email/newsletters” references in Work Experience; avoid restating channel ownership here.
- “Engagement” is broad and may duplicate “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies unless tied specifically to email/member platforms.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete outputs you can quantify.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function supporting web, email, social and video operations.”
- Add measurable outputs if available: number of livestreams/events produced, frequency of video updates, size of web refresh, email volume, or team/process improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and foreground outcomes: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day publishing workflows.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” rather than implying broader management.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; differentiate this as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this at a tactical execution level.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch and frame the rest as program/policy support to keep the progression clear.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Supported innovation and research initiatives for NACo programs and policy teams, translating project work into digital and multimedia communications.”
- Add a second sentence focused on the differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcomes: number of episodes, audience growth, stakeholder groups served, or types of research/projects coordinated.
- Tighten wording by removing vague phrases like “contributed to” and “materials”; use stronger verbs such as “produced,” “developed,” or “managed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing general digital content production; later roles already cover web, video, and multimedia leadership in much stronger terms.
- Don’t repeat “first podcast” elsewhere unless you can show broader organizational impact here.
